newsitem.title: USA: Hussein postpones U.S. visit after Clinton injury.
newsitem.headline: Hussein postpones U.S. visit after Clinton injury.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein has postponed a visit to the United States due to start next week, partly because of disruption caused by a knee injury suffered by President Bill Clinton, the White House said on Friday.

The king's visit is part of a series of trips to Washington by regional leaders seeking a way forward in the Middle East peace process, which has been seriously threatened by renewed Israeli-Palestinian tensions.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters: "Partly because of King Hussein's schedule and obviously partly now because of the president's schedule both the Jordanian side and the U.S. side felt it was better to postpone King Hussein's scheduled visit here to Washington on Monday."

The king, who was due to meet Clinton on Tuesday, cut short a visit to Spain on Thursday to cope with a new crisis after a lone Jordanian soldier shot and killed seven Israeli schoolgirls on the Jordanian-Israeli border.

Clinton underwent surgery on Friday afternoon after tearing the tendon on his right knee when he slipped down some steps during a visit to Florida. He said he intended to go ahead with a summit meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki next Wednesday, but officials said a final decision on that would only be made after the surgery.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak have conferred with Clinton in Washington in recent weeks.
